title: Pre-R∗ Spaces: Structural Properties, Counterexamples, and Applications to Digital Topology
content: We study the interaction between preopen sets, preclosure, and p-boundedness in the theory of pre-R∗ spaces. After recalling the basic definitions, we establish elementary criteria for pre-R∗, derive a finite-space test, and formulate a boundary-obstruction theorem applicable to digital topology. We explain the obstruction that occurs in the digital line and develop a neighborhood-based framework for investigating the digital plane (Z2, k2). The paper distinguishes established results from deductions proved here. In particular, known hereditary and finite-product properties are attributed to earlier work. The digital-plane classification is formulated as a research problem because the generalized-open-set relations alone do not determine the required preclosure and boundedness calculations. Applications to finite digital images and finite-state topological models are discussed.
